items.t: Why Is BlackRock (BLK) Up 8.6% Since Last Earnings Report?
sum: It has been about a month since the last earnings report for BlackRock (BLK). Shares have added about 8.6% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.

Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is BlackRock due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at the latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent drivers for BlackRock before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.
BlackRock's third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $15.93 per share surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $13.97. The figure reflects a 38% rise from the year-ago quarter.
Results benefited from higher revenues, record AUM balance and improved operating performance. However, higher expenses weighed on results.
Net income attributable to BlackRock (on a GAAP basis) was $1.66 billion, up 25% year over year.

Quarterly revenues (on a GAAP basis) were $7.75 billion, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $7.46 billion. The figure increased 19% year over year. The improvement was driven by organic base fee growth, favorable market conditions, higher performance fees and increased technology services revenues.

Investment advisory, administration fees and securities lending revenues were $6.04 billion, up 20% year over year. The increase was primarily driven by organic base fee growth and the positive impact of market movements on average AUM. Securities lending revenues climbed to $253 million from $203 million a year ago.

sum: - BlackRock rose 0.68% to $1,234.70, just $7.42 below its $1,242.12 all-time high.
- Third-quarter EPS jumped 38% to $15.93 on $7.75 billion in revenue, up 19%.
- BlackRock took in $205 billion in Q3 net inflows, with organic base fees up 11%.

BlackRock (BLK) moved against the market on Thursday. By late morning in New York, the stock traded at $1,234.70, up $8.39 or 0.68% from Wednesday’s $1,226.31 close. It opened at $1,230.00, traded between $1,222.50 and $1,235.27, and held its gains while the S&P 500 fell 0.41% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.63% after Nvidia’s CEO resigned. Volume reached 303,465 shares by late morning, against a full-day average of 739,052.

The stock sits right below its record. The 52-week high is $1,242.12, just $7.42 or 0.6% above Thursday’s price. The 52-week low of $917.39 came during the spring private-credit selloff. From that low, BlackRock has gained 34.6%. Over the past 50 sessions, it has traded between $1,038.10 and $1,225.33, so Thursday’s price is already above the top of that range.

The year-to-date numbers show a steady climb. BlackRock began 2026 at $1,070.73. At $1,234.70, it is up 15.3% for the year. Market value has risen 19.1% over 12 months. On 154.42 million shares outstanding, the company is worth $190.7 billion.

The thesis of this forecast is direct. BlackRock has turned from a public-markets index giant into a combined public and private asset manager, and its earnings are now growing faster than at any point in years. Third-quarter earnings per share rose 38% to $15.93. Net inflows hit $205 billion in a single quarter. The operating margin expanded 320 basis points to 47.8%. Private markets, built through the HPS, GIP and Preqin acquisitions, are adding fees that public index funds cannot match. The stock trades at 19.4 times its third-quarter earnings run rate, a multiple that does not yet reflect that shift.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin itself has been under pressure. The price has hovered in the $73,000 to $74,000 range.

- What if you looked at BlackRock through its earnings instead? See why BlackRock's 27.1x P/E tells a different valuation story.
The stock's next move may depend on whether the returns BlackRock earns on its capital are strong enough to justify where the share price has now settled.
If you want to stress test the same question BlackRock faces about whether returns on capital justify the share price, scan a wider field using 33 high quality undervalued stocks.

The Excess Returns model looks at how much profit BlackRock earns above its cost of equity and then capitalizes that gap. BlackRock is modeled with a Book Value of $375.99 per share and a Stable Book Value of $403.84 per share, which signals an equity base that analysts expect to keep compounding rather than shrinking away. On those forecasts, Stable EPS of $69.73 per share compares against a Cost of Equity of $32.25 per share, leaving an Excess Return of $37.48 per share.

OMV Draws a 5% BlackRock Stake as Analysts Diverge on Targets and Ratings
sum: BlackRock has crossed the 5% reporting threshold in OMV, according to a voting rights notification published roughly a week ago. The aggregate position stood at exactly 5.00% of voting rights, split between 4.53% held through shares and 0.47% through financial and other instruments — meaning the disclosed stake was not built entirely on directly held equity.

The ownership disclosure lands amid a busy stretch for the Austrian oil and gas group, which has spent the past fortnight revising its full-year guidance upward while sell-side analysts stake out sharply different positions on the stock.

OMV's third-quarter 2026 results, reported around two weeks ago, showed CCS operating profit before special items of EUR 2.117 billion — a 68% jump on the same quarter a year earlier. Clean CCS net income attributable to shareholders reached EUR 1.15 billion, up 94% year on year. Management pointed to a strong refining business as the principal driver of the earnings surge.

Alongside the numbers, the company lifted its 2026 outlook. Organic capital expenditure is now planned at around EUR 3.5 billion, the Brent price assumption has been raised to above USD 95/bbl, and the expected European refinery reference margin now sits at roughly USD 25/bbl.

Analysts have been adjusting their models to the new guidance — but not their convictions. HSBC on Tuesday reportedly raised its price target on OMV from EUR 63 to EUR 66 while reaffirming its "Reduce" rating, keeping a cautious stance despite the higher valuation marker. UBS moved the other way in spirit on 30 October, lifting its target from EUR 77 to EUR 79 and maintaining its "Buy" recommendation following the quarterly release.

Morgan Stanley took a third path. The US bank reportedly downgraded OMV to "Underweight" on Friday, even as it raised its price target from EUR 65.50 to EUR 67.00 — a combination that pairs a more negative rating with a higher fair-value estimate. OMV shares slipped 0.7% on Friday to close at EUR 71.60, though no clear link between that move and the downgrade can be established.
Further out, OMV is looking to the Black Sea for a fresh earnings stream.

Bitcoin ETFs: Wall Street Yanks $403M From BlackRock's Bitcoin Fund but Retail Keeps Backing AlphaPepe
sum: BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF loses $403M as AlphaPepe keeps drawing retail buyers before public exchange launch

AlphaPepe https://www.alphapepe.io/ has a very different story to tell. Its team reports more than 100 new buyers joining daily, and the presale has raised over $3.31 million. While Wall Street debates Bitcoin's next recovery, ALPE is still available before its first public exchange chart. Retail buyers have not been waiting for a giant fund to tell them when to enter.

The November 6 ETF outflow was driven largely by investors redeeming shares in BlackRock's fund, not BlackRock deciding to abandon Bitcoin. Fidelity's competing fund even recorded inflows. Still, $403 million leaving a single Bitcoin ETF is hardly the picture of effortless institutional demand.

Bitcoin already has global recognition, mature markets and years of price discovery. That makes it a familiar trade, not an early one. AlphaPepe's attraction is the part Bitcoin can no longer offer: a presale allocation before public trading begins, while its community is still forming.

AlphaPepe https://www.alphapepe.io/ has more than 13,000 holders, with over 100 joining each day. Those are the figures drawing attention during a market pullback. Instead of following a famous ticker through another cycle of selling and recovery, these buyers are taking positions in ALPE before an exchange chart even exists. The presale has already collected over $3.31 million. Stage 20 sold out, and Stage 21 is now priced at $0.03611. ALPE lists from $0.08, giving the current presale allocation an announced listing benchmark more than double its entry price. Buyers entering a later stage receive fewer base tokens for the same capital as stage prices increase.

That price difference is only the opening chapter of the bigger-gains argument. A 100x move from $0.03611 would value ALPE at $3.611. At that level, a $1,000 purchase would be worth $100,000. It is a clear illustration of the return early-stage traders chase, not an outcome any presale can promise. The current draw is simpler: the market has not yet opened ALPE to public price discovery.
The daily holder additions give this argument a human face.

Commerzbank stock week: record profit meets new BlackRock position
sum: Commerzbank entered the weekend with a stronger weekly close after its record nine-month result and a new voting-rights filing by BlackRock. The bank's shares closed at EUR 38.21 on Xetra on Friday, November 6, up 1.14% from the Xetra close of Friday, October 30. On Lang & Schwarz, Commerzbank stock traded at EUR 38.13 at 12:06 CET on Saturday, November 7, 0.21% below the Xetra close of Friday, November 6. The quote is available through the real-time quote of Commerzbank stock.

Commerzbank reported on Thursday, November 5, that third-quarter net profit rose 45% year on year to EUR 859 million. Revenue increased 9% to EUR 3.2 billion, while operating profit climbed 25% to EUR 1.31 billion, according to Investing.com, which republished Reuters content.

Net profit for the first nine months reached a record EUR 2.67 billion, up 41%, while operating profit rose 17% to EUR 4.04 billion. Commerzbank confirmed its 2026 target of at least EUR 3.4 billion in net profit and revenue guidance of about EUR 13.2 billion.

The bank reduced its 2026 net interest income outlook to about EUR 8.5 billion from EUR 8.6 billion. Management cited stronger competition for deposits, while maintaining its target for a return on tangible equity of around 12% and a cost-income ratio of 53%.

A voting-rights filing published on Friday, November 6, said BlackRock crossed the relevant threshold on November 3. Its total position in Commerzbank reached 4.44%, comprising 2.98% of voting rights attached to shares and 1.47% through instruments, according to Markets Insider.

The filing listed 2.89% in indirect voting rights attached to shares, alongside lending and contract-for-difference positions. The notification reports holdings and does not by itself establish BlackRock's trading direction or investment intent.
The bank reiterated plans to return about EUR 3.2 billion to shareholders in 2026, keeping capital distribution in focus as investors assess the effect of deposit pricing on future interest income.

Why BlackRock (BLK) is a Top Dividend Stock for Your Portfolio
sum: Getting big returns from financial portfolios, whether through stocks, bonds, ETFs, other securities, or a combination of all, is an investor's dream. But when you're an income investor, your primary focus is generating consistent cash flow from each of your liquid investments.

While cash flow can come from bond interest or interest from other types of investments, income investors hone in on dividends. A dividend is that coveted distribution of a company's earnings paid out to shareholders, and investors often view it by its dividend yield, a metric that measures the dividend as a percent of the current stock price. Many academic studies show that dividends make up large portions of long-term returns, and in many cases, dividend contributions surpass one-third of total returns.

Headquartered in New York, BlackRock (BLK) is a Finance stock that has seen a price change of 1.87% so far this year. The investment firm is currently shelling out a dividend of $5.73 per share, with a dividend yield of 2.1%. This compares to the Financial - Investment Management industry's yield of 2.88% and the S&P 500's yield of 1.34%.

Looking at dividend growth, the company's current annualized dividend of $22.92 is up 10% from last year. Over the last 5 years, BlackRock has increased its dividend 5 times on a year-over-year basis for an average annual increase of 7.33%. Looking ahead, future dividend growth will be dependent on earnings growth and payout ratio, which is the proportion of a company's annual earnings per share that it pays out as a dividend. BlackRock's current payout ratio is 45%, meaning it paid out 45% of its trailing 12-month EPS as dividend.
BLK is expecting earnings to expand this fiscal year as well. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 is $55.63 per share, with earnings expected to increase 15.68% from the year ago period.

Investors like dividends for many reasons; they greatly improve stock investing profits, decrease overall portfolio risk, and carry tax advantages, among others. However, not all companies offer a quarterly payout.

For instance, it's a rare occurrence when a tech start-up or big growth business offers its shareholders a dividend. It's more common to see larger companies with more established profits give out dividends.

items.t: Why Two BlackRock Competitors Told Clients to Buy It
sum: Traders have started betting on a rebound in the world's largest asset manager, BlackRock since its July earnings beat. They are doing it while the BlackRock stock price falls, and weeks after two of the firm's biggest rivals told clients to buy.
JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley both lifted their targets on July 16, and the market ignored them for eleven days.
The put-call ratio weighs bets on a falling share price against bets on a rising one. A reading under 1.00 means the upside bets are winning.
On BlackRock stock, that measure sat at 1.00 on the day of the July 15 results, an even split. By July 24 it had slipped to 0.98, tipping the balance toward a rise.
This particular reading only counts positions traders still hold after the market closes. That makes it the money people are willing to leave on the table overnight.
Short-term traders are less convinced. Counting only the trades placed each day, the same ratio climbed from roughly 0.70 to 0.83, so more downside bets are changing hands than before the results.
The split makes sense. Traders are keeping their bets on a recovery while paying for protection to survive the wait, because the share price has kept sliding.

sum: How exciting is the opportunity for you as well as for investors in SIFs?
We see the category itself as a really interesting one. It fulfills a certain need for a certain segment of investors. Let me explain a bit more.

If you've got a more affluent type of investor who already has the more vanilla exposures to equity and debt markets, and is looking for more outcome-oriented solutions — some of them could be, for example, a higher level of total return but with much lower risk than equities. These are the kinds of outcomes you can construct using a SIF.
The fact that derivatives are allowed, and you can mix and match different asset classes, makes it super interesting for us as manufacturers to create differentiated outcomes.

Once we made the analysis of where within the different categories we think we can provide the most value, we landed on the hybrid category. The Hybrid Long-Short strategy is where we believe the value is strongest. That's the first one we're launching. Once we do that, we'll expand and launch other strategies as well.

We've already got a pretty strong platform to do that. We have the investments team in place. Our active equity process — Systematic Active Equity — is data- and AI-driven, powered by our technology platform Aladdin, and it's already been rolled out in the mutual fund space. We have a Flexicap Fund, a Large Cap Fund, a Sector Rotation Fund. The equity sleeve within the SIF is also going to employ those strategies, with derivatives enabled on top for risk management — which is really the key goal for the use of derivatives. Then you mix and match that with fixed income and REITs, and you can construct some really interesting return streams from a total return perspective.

The framework is the same — the same overall people, platform, and process. But the fact that this asset class allows you to do more means we're going to be leveraging our insight and expertise on the options side. We have that in-house; we have the capabilities and the technology to do that.

sum: Picture this: Right now, a broker at a fancy Manhattan firm violently clicks his mouse, liquidating positions and helping drag $171 million out of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs in a single afternoon.
Meanwhile, a guy in Ohio opens an app like SoFi and quietly buys $50 of physical Bitcoin while waiting for his dog to go to the bathroom before bed.
These two investors are trading the exact same asset, but they are playing two completely different games.

For years, buying Bitcoin meant leaving the familiar, regulated world of brokerage accounts and stepping into the digital Wild West of crypto exchanges, private keys and hardware wallets. Then Wall Street did what Wall Street does best: It took a radical, anti-bank asset, stuffed it into a corporate wrapper, and slapped a management fee on it.
Spot Bitcoin ETFs now hold nearly $135 billion in total assets. If you are looking to get exposure without learning the plumbing, they are the ultimate “easy button.”
But before you tap buy, you need to know exactly what you’re giving up for that convenience.
The pitch for a Bitcoin ETF is almost intentionally boring. You open your standard brokerage account, type in a ticker symbol (like BlackRock’s IBIT or Fidelity’s FBTC), and buy shares.

Is IBIT a Good Investment in 2026? What You Should Know About BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF
sum: For decades, traditional investors watched Bitcoin’s explosive growth from the sidelines, deterred by the complexities of digital wallets, private keys, and unregulated platforms. IBIT changed everything by wrapping physical Bitcoin into a familiar, heavily regulated, and easily tradable Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF). While BlackRock offers unprecedented convenience and security, buying a Bitcoin ETF is fundamentally different from owning real cryptocurrency.

In this comprehensive guide, we will break down the exact mechanics of IBIT, weigh its pros and cons against holding native Bitcoin, and help you decide if it aligns with your 2026 investment strategy.
IBIT is a "spot" ETF, meaning it holds physical Bitcoin to accurately track the asset's real-time market price, rather than relying on complex futures contracts.
It allows you to gain exposure to Bitcoin directly through your standard traditional brokerage or retirement accounts without ever needing to manage a crypto wallet or seed phrase.
Backed by BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, it heavily mitigates the risk of losing your investment to lost passwords or individual exchange hacks.
Unlike the native crypto market, which operates 24/7, IBIT is strictly bound by traditional stock market hours. You cannot buy the dip or sell a crash on weekends or holidays.
Holding IBIT incurs an ongoing annual management fee, which will slowly eat into your long-term profits compared to holding native Bitcoin yourself.

BlackRock curbs redemptions at HPS private credit fund as investors weigh risks
sum: BlackRock has moved to cap investor withdrawals from a flagship private credit vehicle, underscoring growing stress in a corner of the market that many wealth firms have leaned on for yield and diversification.
The asset manager said Friday it is limiting redemptions at the HPS Corporate Lending Fund after a jump in investors asking for their money back.

As reported first by the Financial Times, the fund, which manages about $26 billion, received roughly $1.2 billion in withdrawal requests in the first quarter, or about 9.3% of its net asset value. It will pay out $620 million, hitting a 5% quarterly threshold that allows BlackRock to restrict further redemptions under the fund’s terms.
BlackRock shares fell in early trading after the news, extending a slide that has tracked rising concern about private credit exposures.

The move follows steps by other large players: Earlier this week, it was revealed that Blackstone moved past its usual 5% redemption cap to 7% amid a surge of investor requests; the firm and its employees also invested $400 million to help honor investor requests, according to Reuters. Last month, Blue Owl also shifted the mechanism for payouts in its Blue Owl Capital Corp. II fund from quarterly tender offers to periodic capital distributions funded by asset sales and repayments.

For advisors and RIAs that have steered clients into private credit funds, the redemption pressure is a reminder that these products sit on top of inherently illiquid loans. Managers promise periodic liquidity, but it's not always possible to sell the underlying corporate debt without significantly impacting prices. That liquidity mismatch becomes more obvious when markets turn volatile or sentiment sours.

HPS Investment Partners, which runs the corporate lending fund, framed the gating decision as a way to keep cash on hand for new deals. “In our judgment, preserving the fund’s available capital to lean into this perceived opportunity set, while providing liquidity to shareholders consistently with the fund’s designed parameters, is in the best interest of the fund as a whole,” it said in a statement reported by Reuters.

items.t: BlackRock Earnings: Market Gains and Record Inflows Drive AUM and Revenue to New Highs
sum: BlackRock BLK ended December 2025 with a record $14.042 trillion in assets under management, up 21.6% year over year and above our estimate of $13.966 trillion. The firm continues to benefit from flows into its passive offerings as well as ongoing market gains.

Why it matters: BlackRock continues to outperform most of its traditional asset management peers from an organic AUM growth perspective, as its mix of index funds and exchange-traded funds appeals more to investors than its active products. The expansion of the firm’s private capital platform has only added to its ability to generate positive flows on a more consistent basis.

- Net long-term inflows of $268 billion in the fourth quarter represented an annualized organic AUM growth rate of 8.6%, well above our annual target of 3%-5%. We expect to see lower growth rates from most of BlackRock’s peers when they report.

- The iShares platform remains the biggest driver of flows for BlackRock. The firm picked up a record $181 billion in net long-term inflows, equivalent to a 13.9% annualized organic AUM growth rate, from its ETF business during the fourth quarter.

The bottom line: While we had expected the back half of 2025 to see increased headwinds for flows and market gains as the impacts of the US government’s fiscal, tariff, and immigration policies became more apparent, BlackRock continued to benefit from ongoing market gains.

- While there was little in wide-moat-rated BlackRock’s fourth-quarter results that would alter our long-term view of the firm, we expect to increase our $1,170 fair value estimate to $1,200 per share as we adjust the baseline for AUM in our valuation model. We view the shares as slightly undervalued right now.

- We do, however, expect to remain conservative with our near-term assumptions for BlackRock and the rest of the US-based asset managers. We believe that governmental policies put in place this past year will eventually affect the equity and fixed-income markets.
